 Follow Us On: News Movies Celebrities Hanuman Ansh director calls Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana a 'cultural renaissance' Hanuman Ansh director calls Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana a 'cultural renaissance'
 In an exclusive interview with India Today, Hanuman Ansh director Vishal Chaturvedi called director Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Rise of a Legend as part of a "cultural renaissance." He also addressed his Goswami Tulsidas biopic overlap with Dr Chandraprakash Dwivedi.
 Advertisement Hanuman Ansh director Vishal Chaturvedi, speaking exclusively to India Today, expressed optimism about Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana. (Credit: Instagram/filmervishal/T-Series) By: Anurag Singh Bohra New Delhi , Nov 20, 2026 16:59 IST Last Updated Nov 20, 2026 16:59 IST Published by Anurag Bohra Nov 20, 2026 16:59 IST Director Vishal Chaturvedi is optimistic about more devotional films on Lord Rama and Goswami Tulsidas being made. In an exclusive interview with India Today, the Hanuman Ansh director linked director Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Rise of a Legend to a "cultural renaissance." While the Ranbir Kapoor-Sai Pallavi film has sparked an ongoing debate over its massive scale and Rs 1,500-crore box-office haul so far, Chaturvedi highlighted that visual spectacle is just as essential as good writing.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Hanuman Ansh has been praised for depicting the life story of saint Neem Karori Baba and his devotion to Lord Hanuman. When asked about his views on the recently released epic drama Ramayana : Rise of a Legend, which not only depicts the legend of Lord Rama but is also associated with a massive budget and earnings, Chaturvedi expressed excitement about the film.
 He said, "I am going to watch the film at the very first opportunity. I am trying to find the time so that I can definitely watch this film. I am very excited and looking forward to watching the film. Since, I have not seen it yet, so I won't be able to comment on it. But they have also made a film about Lord Rama. I came to know about all the cheers during the Hanuman Ji scene. I wish that films like that work."
 Expressing happiness about such films being made, he added, "I hope such films work for good and the cultural renaissance of such films is very important."
 Chaturvedi, who made Hanuman Ansh without any big stars, was asked about the ongoing debate over whether budgets or content matter more in making a film successful. He said, "I think, firstly, there is writing in the content. There is nothing beyond writing. What you have written in the paper is what matters. If what you have written is not good, then other things don't work. But if it is good, then other things can lead to exponential growth. So, first, the story should be written well in the paper. You should pay attention to that. You should pay attention to the content."
 While emphasising making Hanuman Ansh with a moderate budget, he also reflected on the relevance of "visual spectacle" and its scale.
 "You should pay attention to the words and expressions of the dialogue. All of that should be the primary thing. The rest of the things, the scale, the visual spectacle of the film, should also be there if you can afford it. If you can't afford it, then make the film as it is. Make the film with simplicity. People will like it. And our film, I guess, proved to be effective. It was a small-budget film, but the result was of a big budget," the director added.
 advertisement There was a recent announcement about both Chaturvedi and Dr Chandra Prakash Dwivedi (separetly) making a film on the life of bhakti-poet Goswami Tulsidas , the writer of the epic poem, Ramcharitmanas based on Ramayana . As Chaturvedi and Dwivedi introduced the film's poster on the very same day, with the same title – RamBola , the former feels that there is "so much on Tulsidas ji" that even making "10 films on him" would be less.
 Chaturvedi said, "I believe that it is a story of the public domain, about which anyone can make a film. We are working on the subject. There can be so much on Tulsidas ji that even if we make 10 films on him, there will be less. So we are making our own film, and he will make his own film and I wish him well. It would be good if you could see Tulsidas ji from two perspectives. You will know more about him."
 When asked about the recent statement by Chaturvedi and producer Namrata G Singh over the rights and publicity arrangements of Hanuman Ansh , the director feels it was necessary to prevent people from making false speculations about the film's OTT and satellite release.
 advertisement While reflecting on the importance of timely clarification on such issues to the audience, Chaturvedi said, "We did it very late. But we did it when we felt there was worldwide chatter. In such a situation, people start to talk on our behalf in the market. They started talking about OTT. Everyone says that we know this or that. But there is an authorised channel whose signatures we talk to. We need to clarify that."
 "We didn't say anything at the conflict level. But later, people are talking on our behalf. That is why we put this statement so that everyone knows that we are dealing with OTT and satellite. In such a situation, we wanted to clarify so that there is no confusion," he added. Films on religious figures often face intense social media scrutiny and backlash over public sentiments and faith. When asked whether he worried about such controversies while making Hanuman Ansh , Chaturvedi emphasised that sticking strictly to primary sources and factual reference points was his biggest safeguard, noting that any spiritual subject or biopic demands sensitivity rather than relying on negative publicity. "Any religious or spiritual subject should be dealt with a lot of sensitivity and sensibility. Otherwise, if you want to run a film with controversy, then you are stuck. Gone are those days when you could make a film successful by using controversy. Negativity cannot bring any positivity. So, if you genuinely want to talk heart-to-heart, you focus on the narrative and try to make the facts a reference point. All the scenes of our film have a reference point," he said. Hanuman Ansh turned cinema halls into a deeply devotional experience during its theatrical run. When asked about his expectations ahead of the film's OTT release, Chaturvedi noted that the project drew several first-time theatregoers, while many others — especially those dealing with health conditions or living in smaller towns without cinema halls—missed out on watching it on the big screen. "There are many families who live in small places and they don't have a theatre. Or they couldn't see the film due to some circumstances. So, our idea is to reach as many people as possible," he said, adding, "You must have heard that many people have watched the film again and again. So, people who want to watch the film again and again will watch it. There is a large population who want to watch the film. We are very happy about this. We want everyone to watch the film together with their families from November 27 onwards." Hanuman Ansh is set to premiere on SonyLiv on November 27, 2026. - Ends Must Watch
